title: Bowel ultrasound
what: The doctor looks at the walls of your bowel through your belly using ultrasound. It shows inflammation, thickening, and bowel loops.
why: For belly pain, suspected appendicitis, bowel inflammation, to follow long-term bowel conditions, and in children, for pain and vomiting.
duration: usually 20 to 30 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: Where your belly hurts and for how long
If you recently had a colonoscopy or a barium X-ray
If you have a bowel condition, bring your reports

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually do not eat for 4 to 6 hours. Sometimes you are asked to drink water before. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Gas
prepare.text: The day before: eat less gassy food: cabbage, beans, fizzy drinks, dark rye bread.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: You lie on your back and uncover your belly
Gel is put on your skin
The probe is moved over your whole belly, sometimes with a little pressure
Sometimes you are asked to turn on your side
feel: Cool gel and pressure from the probe
If a spot is sore, the pressure may be unpleasant. Tell the doctor
after: You can eat and drink right away
The report is usually ready right away
The doctor may order more tests
red_flags: Severe, worsening belly pain with vomiting or fever: call emergency services

faq.q: Does a bowel ultrasound replace a colonoscopy?
faq.a: No. Ultrasound sees the bowel wall from outside, but it cannot see small polyps inside.

faq.q: Why can't I eat before the ultrasound?
faq.a: After eating, there is more gas in the bowel, and gas blocks the ultrasound.

reminders.text: Bowel ultrasound tomorrow. Today, no cabbage, beans, or fizzy drinks. Do not eat for the time the clinic told you.
